read_sections: Appendix A.2 proof, A.3 implementation, A.4 DAVE composition

claim_evidence.claim: Opposing residual branches make the standard epsilon-rule divide by a small residual output and create large opposing branch relevances. Forward cancellation alone does not force relevance explosion when downstream relevance is zero.

For residual branches a,b with a+b nonzero and gamma positive, a sign-consistent gamma weighting bounds each redistribution factor between -1/gamma and 1+1/gamma. The symmetric factors sum to one, yielding conservation and |R_a|+|R_b| <= (1+2/gamma)|R_out| per residual merge.
Authors explicitly restrict guarantees to residual additions and call them structural, not faithfulness guarantees. Full-model attribution quality is tested empirically.
Proof explicitly excludes exact cancellation a+b=0; two cases prove the bound. Do not silently extend this proposition to all zero-output inputs.
ResLRP can compose with DAVE spatial translation processing because residual amplification and pixel patch artifacts concern different stages.

research_evidence.thesis_comparison: Directly relevant to Chapter 7 ViT attribution and stability. It stabilizes backward residual redistribution on the original trained transformer. This differs from stabilizing cancellation between forward convex streams in Chapters 3/7, and from comparing normalized trajectory laws with Hellinger in Chapter 11. It does not give a full forward DC construction or game-equilibrium representation.

placement.anchor: Related Work: Interpretability in Transformers; after DAVE/registers discussion

research_evidence.minimal_tex: ResLRP targets another source of ViT attribution instability: cancellation between residual branches, using a residual $\gamma$-rule with conservation and a local bound on relevance amplification \parencite{Berend2026ResLRP}.
research_evidence.optional_precise_expansion_tex: For nonzero residual outputs and $\gamma>0$, its bound $\lvert R_{\mathrm{in}}\rvert+\lvert R_{\mathrm{up}}\rvert\le(1+2/\gamma)\lvert R_{\mathrm{out}}\rvert$ concerns one backward residual merge; it does not certify faithfulness or stable evaluation of a forward DC split.
limits: Preprint, not a peer-reviewed 2026 venue claim.
Do not conflate local absolute relevance amplification with normalized trajectory distance or numerical forward-DC cancellation.

claim_evidence.claim: LRPx formulates LRP/AttnLRP using modified Gradient-times-Input and stop-gradient changes that leave forward evaluated outputs unchanged. Half-gradient product rule recovers equal relevance split.
Linear-layer equivalence is derived with epsilon=0. Do not imply equality with the thesis nonzero-epsilon or generalized alpha-beta rule from this argument.

For an elementwise activation g, x*detach(g(x)/x) preserves forward value and recovers the LRP identity redistribution through modified Gradient-times-Input; GELU/SiLU are explicitly mentioned and zero input handled separately.
detach(gate)*signal implements the signal-take-all product rule, attributing nothing to gate and all incoming relevance to signal.
LayerNorm freezes standard deviation but retains differentiable linear mean-centering. This is not the thesis implementation, which freezes both mean and scale.
AttnLRP softmax redistribution is equivalent to Gradient-times-Input at that layer; it does not freeze attention.

Subject-verb agreement attribution performance varies across BERT/GPT2/Llama3 families and metrics. Ground-truth subjects are automatically parsed and may be noisy; this is not a general causal faithfulness certificate.

research_evidence.thesis_comparison: Supplies a direct implementation-level reference for the thesis GELU gate detachment. It also clarifies fixed-attention LRP versus AttnLRP. It does not prove the thesis composite alpha-beta Value rule, the game semantics, or a forward convex split.

placement.anchor: Implementation details, GELU gate detachment paragraph, after formula x Phi(c)

research_evidence.minimal_tex: This is the modified Gradient$\times$Input implementation of the LRP identity rule for elementwise activations derived by \textcite[Appendix~D.3]{Arras2025CloseLook}.
research_evidence.alternative_related_work_tex: \textcite{Arras2025CloseLook} make the implementation distinction explicit by deriving LRP and AttnLRP rules from modified Gradient$\times$Input calculations and comparing them with ALTI-Logit on a subject--verb agreement benchmark.
limits: Do not claim equivalence to all thesis alpha-beta/stabilized rules.
Their LayerNorm retains mean-centering; thesis freezes mean as well.

paper_evidence.finding: Analyzes singular values of the normalized output-to-input attribution redistribution matrix at a fixed input. Its leading singular value bounds amplification, while collapsed later singular values impair target discrimination.
Defines the stability–sensitivity metric from the singular spectrum and bounds layerwise LRP-gamma operator growth under its assumptions.

Experiments on MNIST and ImageNet VGG-16 illustrate stability–target-sensitivity trade-offs for LRP gamma and SmoothGrad. Spectral, pixel-flipping, and entropy measures do not agree on all optimal parameter values.

research_evidence.limitation: Their operator amplification criterion at a fixed input should not be described as the same property as Maximum Sensitivity to input perturbations. No equivalence with trajectory Hellinger distance is proved.

verified_claims.claim: The paper instantiates fidelity, understandability, and sufficiency for visual counterfactual explanations. Fidelity asks for plausible transformations and a robust classifier response; understandability emphasizes semantic sparsity; sufficiency motivates diverse counterfactuals.
SCE combines diffusion-based projection, a smoothed distilled surrogate, sparsification, and diversification; generated input transformations are distinct from a plot of a local stream derivative.
The paper evaluates counterfactual properties and model-improvement actionability, with heterogeneous results across models and datasets.

recommended_placement.anchor: Establishing whether these patterns support reliable counterfactual explanations requires interventions on the complete model.
recommended_placement.action: Append one sentence immediately after the anchor, in DCINNs at scale.
recommended_placement.latex: Such an evaluation could draw on the fidelity, understandability, and sufficiency criteria developed for visual counterfactual explainers \parencite{Bender2026Desiderata}.
recommended_placement.rationale: The preceding sentence already states the unresolved obligation to test complete-model interventions; this citation supplies concrete assessment criteria without claiming those obligations have been met.

alternative_placement.note: Could instead follow the stream-sensitivity qualification with the same forward-looking evaluation sentence. Use one location to avoid redundancy.

avoid_claims: Do not say this paper proves either DCINN stream is factual/counterfactual, establishes feature necessity, or converts a local derivative into a finite class-changing intervention.
